blueprint.summary: Scratch Pad is a single-note app: the user types into one text area, the text is saved automatically one second after typing stops, the text can be saved to a Markdown file the user chooses, a plain text file the user chooses can replace the text after confirmation, and the text is stored on the device and restored after restart.
targetUsers: People who want one always-available scratch note for quick jottings
Writers who keep a single running draft and occasionally export it as Markdown
goals: Provide one text area for a single note
Persist the note automatically one second after typing stops
Save the note to a user-chosen Markdown file
Replace the note from a user-chosen plain text file after confirmation
Restore the stored note after restart
nonGoals: Multiple notes or a note list
Rich text formatting or Markdown preview

features.name: Single note editor
features.userOutcome: The user types freely in one text area and the note is kept on the device and restored after restart.
features.trigger: The user types in the text area, or the app starts.
features.behavior: The main window shows exactly one text area holding the single note. On app start the stored note is loaded into the text area; if no note has been stored yet the text area is empty. Every keystroke updates the in-memory text, and one second after the last keystroke the full text is written to the device store, replacing the previous stored text. If the user types again before the one-second delay elapses, the pending save is restarted so only the latest text is written. The text area accepts any text including empty text; saving empty text stores an empty note. If loading the stored note fails, the text area is shown empty and one error message states the note could not be loaded.
features.failureOutcome: A failed automatic save leaves the previously stored note unchanged and one error message states the note could not be saved; the text stays in the text area so the next pause in typing retries the save.
acceptanceSignals: After typing text and advancing the injected clock by 1000 ms, reading the stored note returns exactly the typed text.
Typing more text 500 ms after a change and advancing the clock by 1000 ms stores only the latest text, not the intermediate text.
With a stored note present, starting the app shows that stored text in the text area.
When the store write fails, the previously stored note read back is unchanged and the error message is shown.

features.name: Save note as Markdown file
features.userOutcome: The user saves the current note text to a Markdown file at a location the user chooses.
features.trigger: The user activates the Save as Markdown control.
features.behavior: Activating the control opens a Save panel where the user chooses the destination and file name; the suggested file name is scratch-pad.md. The file is written as Markdown with a level-one heading line '# Scratch Pad', one blank line, then the note text exactly as it appears in the text area, with no trailing newline added beyond the note text. The write replaces the whole file atomically so a failed write leaves any existing file at that location unchanged. On success a confirmation message states the file was saved. If the user cancels the Save panel nothing is written and no message is shown.
features.failureOutcome: If the file cannot be written, the existing file at the chosen location is left unchanged and one error message states the file could not be saved.
acceptanceSignals: Saving a note whose text is 'Hello' produces a file whose content is '# Scratch Pad\n\nHello'.
Saving an empty note produces a file whose content is '# Scratch Pad\n\n'.
When the write fails, a pre-existing file at the chosen location still has its previous content.
Cancelling the Save panel writes no file and shows no message.

features.name: Open plain text file to replace note
features.userOutcome: The user replaces the note text with the contents of a plain text file the user chooses, after confirming.
features.trigger: The user activates the Open text file control.
features.behavior: Activating the control opens an Open panel where the user chooses a plain text file. After a file is chosen, a confirmation dialog asks 'Replace the current note with the contents of this file?' with the labels Replace and Cancel. Choosing Cancel leaves the note text unchanged and writes nothing. Choosing Replace reads the file as UTF-8 text, puts that text into the text area, and immediately stores it as the note, replacing the previous stored text. If the file cannot be read as UTF-8 text, the note text is left unchanged and one error message states the file could not be opened.
features.failureOutcome: If the chosen file cannot be read, the note text and the stored note are left unchanged and one error message states the file could not be opened.
acceptanceSignals: Confirming Replace with a file containing 'Draft two' leaves the text area showing 'Draft two' and reading the stored note returns 'Draft two'.
Choosing Cancel in the confirmation dialog leaves the text area and the stored note unchanged.
When the chosen file cannot be read, the text area and the stored note keep their previous values and the error message is shown.

dataObjects.name: Note
dataObjects.purpose: The single note text the user types, stored on the device and restored after restart.
dataObjects.retentionIntent: Kept on the device until the user replaces it by typing or by opening a plain text file.

dataObjects.name: Markdown export file
dataObjects.purpose: A Markdown file the user chooses to save the note text to.
dataObjects.retentionIntent: Kept at the location the user chose until the user removes it outside the app.

qualityRequirements: The automatic save writes the full note text one second after the last keystroke, with no partial text written.
The stored note is restored into the text area when the app starts.
productConstraints: The app holds exactly one note; there is no list of notes.
The note is stored on the device only; no network access is used.
The Markdown export begins with the heading '# Scratch Pad' followed by one blank line and the note text.

polish.quote: Offer a default file name that fits the document, then call the document command with the chosen path; a cancelled dialog changes nothing and shows no error.
polish.why: The open dialog has no default name, and the flow is open, then confirm, then read_text_file. The sentence is boilerplate and implies a save-style flow. A coder can ignore it but may hesitate.
polish.fix: Remove the default-file-name sentence from the Open task prompt, which is generic boilerplate that does not apply.

polish.where: TASKS.md TASK-06 and TASK-07 task prompts
polish.quote: refresh it after your own writes by patching it with the record your command returns (after a delete, remove that id), never by calling a list command
polish.why: The packet has no delete, no list and no per-row control. These clauses are inapplicable, and the 'empty list' clause could be read as making the controls conditionally disabled.
polish.fix: Drop the delete, empty-list and nothing-to-export boilerplate from the task prompts for TASK-06 and TASK-07.

polish.quote: When the write fails, a pre-existing file at the chosen location still has its previous content.
polish.why: The focused test is a TypeScript test with a fake call, so it cannot check file content. Only TASK-02's Rust test can verify this criterion, but the acceptance ID is mapped to OWN-SAVE-NOTE. The agent must guess how the feature test proves it.
polish.fix: Add a short statement to PRD and TRD that the Rust command writes no note data and that the TS test fake only asserts the content string and path, with atomicity proven in datastore_tests.

polish.quote: Text typed within the last second before the window is closed is written before the app exits.
polish.why: The close-flush behaviour is in the PRD UX list and the TASK-05 criteria, but not among the PRD feature acceptance outcomes or the ACC IDs, so it has no traceable ACC.
polish.fix: Add an ACC (for example ACC-SINGLE-NOTE-EDITOR-05) to the PRD and TRD stating that calling flush() stores the latest text without advancing the clock.

polish.quote: If loading the stored note fails, the text area is shown empty and one error message states the note could not be loaded.
polish.why: No acceptance outcome covers this. If the load fails and the user then types, note[] is empty, so the first save calls create_note and adds a second row beside the unreadable stored one. This conflicts with 'exactly one note' and is not specified.
polish.fix: Add an ACC for the load-failure message and state that the first save after a failed load must update the existing row, or that saving is blocked until a retry succeeds.

polish.quote: resolves true when stored, or false after showing the failure message
polish.why: The PRD gives no message for a failed store write after Replace, and the Open task says 'The file could not be opened' only for read failures. The agent must guess which message appears when the file reads fine but the store write fails.
polish.fix: State in TASK-05 and the Open task that a failed replace write shows 'The note could not be saved.' with retry, or the generic notice, explicitly.

polish.quote: writing every date or time it shows in local time (the stored UTC value converted; this is the one time rule for every exported file; its test sets TZ or injects the offset so the exported bytes are deterministic)
polish.why: The export contains no dates. The clause could prompt a pointless TZ-injection requirement in the test. The 'Reject invalid or incomplete records' and 'every stored row' recovery text also does not fit a file contract.
polish.fix: Remove the local-time and 'stored row' boilerplate from CON-DATA-MARKDOWN-EXPORT-FILE, or scope it to 'no dates in this export'.

review.verdict: No blocking defects. The idea maps cleanly to three features with acceptance criteria. Task order is dependency-safe, and the shared-file lines in AGENTS agree with the TASKS create/modify lists. The data contract, commands and wire format are fully specified. The delayed-save case is covered: the TRD names a close-time flush with its owner and mechanism (onCloseRequested, flush()), the kit capability allows destroy, and TASK-05 has a flush criterion. The remaining items are polish: boilerplate that does not apply, and two small spec gaps.
